persona: Polite but firm office manager. Has read her policy schedule and does not accept that she should pay the excess for hail damage while the car was parked. Answers other questions readily.
initial_message: Hello, I want to claim for hail damage to my car. It was parked in the open staff car park at work in Papanui when a hailstorm hit on Tuesday 22 September, and now the bonnet, roof and boot are covered in small dents. Nobody was hurt and the car drives fine. I have read my schedule and I don't think I should have to pay the $750 excess, because the car was parked and the hail was nobody's fault.

facts.incident.description: A short, heavy hailstorm hit Papanui in the afternoon while my car was parked in the uncovered staff car park at work. When I came out after work the bonnet, roof and boot lid were covered in small dents. No glass was broken.
facts.incident.location: Uncovered staff car park at my workplace on Bellbird Test Drive, Papanui, Christchurch
facts.loss.description: Dozens of small hail dents across the bonnet, roof and boot lid; no broken glass
facts.witness.name: Hana Wakathorne
facts.policyholder.name: Ella Rimuvale
facts.vehicle.damage_description: About 35 small dents on the bonnet, about 50 on the roof and about 20 on the boot lid, each 1 to 3 cm across; paint not cracked, no glass damage
facts.if_asked_about_who_was_driving: Nobody. The car was parked and I was inside at work.
facts.if_asked_about_the_witness: My colleague Hana Wakathorne saw the hail hit the cars in the car park from the office window.
facts.if_asked_about_the_excess: My schedule says $750 for each event. I don't think it should apply here, because the car was parked and hail is nobody's fault. I would like someone to look at that.
facts.evidence.photos: A photo of the bonnet taken in the car park when I came out after work, and a photo of the roof taken at home that evening. Both available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Cedar Holt Auto Refinish dated 24 September 2026, total $4,174.50 including GST. Available now.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo of the bonnet of a white sedan parked in an open outdoor car park an hour after a hailstorm, in flat grey overcast light. Dozens of small round dents are spread across the white bonnet, clearly visible as distortions in the reflection of the sky, with small white hailstones melting on the bonnet and on the wet asphalt. The frame shows only the bonnet and the bottom edge of the windscreen, seen from the side at a low angle. No licence plate, no badges, no logos, no text, no people.

materials.purpose: Policy schedule that matches the motor wording in the knowledge base; it states the $750 excess the claimant disputes

design.notes: Professional review without a document conflict: the claimant disputes the $750 excess in her first message. MTR-EXC-01 and MTR-AUTH-01 leave a disputed excess to staff.

triage.rationale: The claimant says in her first message that she does not accept the $750 excess on her schedule, so a claims professional must handle the disputed excess (claimant_disputes_terms, complex). Otherwise simple: parked car, hail, nobody hurt, no other party, car drivable, clear photos and a complete quote at NZD 4,174.50 including GST, policy on file. Allowed: the system may route multi-panel hail damage to an assessor; it does not change the class. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 February 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2016-02-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that hail damage is or is not covered, or that the claim will be paid.

The Agent waives, reduces or removes the excess, says the excess will not apply to hail, or tells the claimant a final excess decision. Explaining that the schedule records a $750 excess for each event is fine.
The Agent acknowledges the claimant's disagreement with the excess and says it will be passed to, or reviewed by, a staff member or claims specialist, without deciding it.

allowed_variation: Whether the Agent quotes the $750 excess from the schedule when acknowledging the disagreement
Whether both photos or only one are requested
